details:
This feature request is so niche that the term "niche" doesn't do it justice. Still, I'll throw it down here just for the sake of shooting my shot.

Recently, VRChat officially adopted toki pona as a language option. Its common writing system, *sitelen Lasina*, uses Latin characters for writing, the typical alphanumeric range like the ones being used to write this post right now that you are looking at. 

However, one of its most frequently used native writing systems is the *sitelen pona*. Its characters live in the Unicode range F1900−F19FF and all symbols are public domain. 

Publicly available fonts, such as my personal preference of Fairfax HD (available at https://www.kreativekorp.com/software/fonts/fairfaxhd/ and licensed under OFL 1.1), support this writing system natively and work very well as fallback fonts. This font in particular supports a *lot* of languages, in fact, check the UCSUR tab at the top of its webpage.

Being able to use this lithography in text chat could be very comfortable for speakers like myself, as it feels natural to read and has higher information density.
title: Integrate UCSUR-compliant fonts for text chat
